content: Gardevoir GX
A playable Gardevoir? Never seen one.
Concept

If Gardevoir isn't top of the meta, is it really a Pokemon format? A contender since its win at the 2017 World Championships, this time the Fairy-Type menace comes with pals Alolan Ninetales GX and Swampert ready to help turn a Gardevoir GX into a OHKO machine. This deck has insane draw, acceleration, recursion, a crazy high HP attacker without a damage cap, hard counters to Ultra Beasts and Spread, two capable single-prize attackers and oh my does Gardevoir not just always have everything?!
The Deck
Decklist on LimitlessTCG
List credit goes to Jimmy Pendarvis and his group at Roanoake Regionals 2018. Modified based on suggestions from Whimsicast.
Pokemon
3-1-(3-1) Ralts, Kirlia, Gardevoir GX & Gardevoir

The Gardevoir line in this deck has a lot going on. Ralt's “Beckon” can be used to recycle critical Guzma and Judge against control decks, but its 50HP makes it more susceptible to a boosted Buzzwole GX “Jet Punch”. Kirlia helps to save rare candies, and the non-GX Gardevoir's “Sensitive Ray” does a solid 160 Damage for [Y][C][C] as a single-prizer when needed, although you'd usually rather be attacking with Gardevoir GX as its absurd 230HP means it isn't likely to get OHKOed.

Speaking of Gardevoir GX, the title card of the deck has 3 relevant attributes that work nicely together. The main attack you'll be using is “Infinite Force”, which scales damage based on the amount of Energy attached to both the attacking Gardevoir GX and the Defending Pokemon. With Gardevoir GX's Ability “Secret Spring” you can ramp said damage efficiently, and although your first Gardevoir GX may not OHKO each attack, the second one should be set up enough that it cuts right through anything in the Active Spot. “Secret Spring” has additional utility though, as you can accelerate anywhere on your board, letting you get cheeky Alolan Ninetales GX or Solgaleo GX attacks in from nought.

The final and maybe most interesting part of Gardevoir GX's arsenal is its GX attack “Twilight GX”. For [Y], you shuffle 10 cards from your Discard pile back into your Deck. This trump card allows you to recycle finite resources like Max Potion & Rare Candy or Energy cards against control decks. Due to Gardevoir GX's 230HP and ramping damage, there are often positions where you know it will not get KOed and you cannot attack for KO, and so can afford to take the turn to use “Twilight GX” and solidify a winning position.
2-1-2 Mudkip, Marshtomp, Swampert

The Swampert line is a neat inclusion. As a draw engine, this deck is looking to find combos of Stage 2 & Rare Candy & Energy in one hand, so “Power Draw” shines at strong dig whilst discarding dead cards from the hand. At 160HP, and as a single-prizer, Swampert is often a low priority target on the Bench, which lets you get away with keeping your draw engine in play for longer.

Notably the Swampert line was included in the deck for its Water Typing. Water-Type Mudkip can be searched via Brooklet Hill, and the Water-Type Swampert can use “Hydro Pump” with a Super Boost Energy {*} (or a DCE, Fairy Energy & Choice Band) to OHKO Blacephalon GX, which Gardevoir GX struggles with.
Swampert standing on the shoulders of giants
2-2 Alolan Vulpix, Alolan Ninetales GX

With the introduction of Alolan Ninetales GX in Lost Thunder, the portion of setup decks moved to a gameplan of using “Beacon” followed by “Mysterious Guidance” to flood their board with Evolution Pokemon as early as turn 2. Gardevoir GX is one of those decks. Brooklet Hill searchable Alolan Vulpix can tutor its evolution and a Gardevoir GX to hand, without even costing an Energy. This can then be followed up with a “Mysterious Guidance” to get 2 Rare Candy, maybe the Timer Ball, anything your heart desires. And from there Alolan Ninetales GX isn't a dead space on the board, it is a capable attacker, softening up targets with “Snowy Wind” and is critical in the Blacephalon GX and Buzzwole GX matchups as “Sublimation GX” OHKOs any Ultra-Beast.
The Alolan Vulpix/Ninetales line
2 Tapu Lele GX

Tapu Lele GX is an Ultra Ball searchable out to any Supporter card in the deck with its “Wonder Tag” Ability. Turn 1 this can grab an Elm's Lecture, or it can fetch the game winning Guzma on the last turn. You can also attack with “Energy Drive” in a pinch, and even further ramp it with Gardevoir GX's “Secret Spring”. As the lowest HP Pokemon GX in the deck, take care to not bench it where unnecessary.
1-0-1 Cosmog, Solgaleo GX

This tech inclusion shores up a number of matchups. Solgaleo GX is another behemoth at 250HP, and “Shining Mane” removes the Weakness on all of your Pokemon in play, drastically improving the decks matchup into Metal-Type decks. Both of its attacks are solid, “Prominence GX” primarily working to bully spread style Shrine of Punishment decks, whilst “Turbo Strike” threatens 2HKOs on most Pokemon GX whilst reloading a threat on your Bench.
Trainers
Elm Brooklet Engine and Setup

Where this deck can struggle is getting set up fast enough that your opponent cannot simply cheese a win by koing evolving Basic Pokemon and then gusting a benched Tapu Lele GX. To ensure as many Pokemon Turn 1 the deck plays a full 4 copies of Professor Elm's Lecture, and the 2 Brooklet Hill help search Mudkip and Alolan Vulpix specifically. Then to evolve said Pokemon it plays a full 4 copies of both Rare Candy and Ultra Ball. For further Mid-Game consistency 3 Cynthia keep you drawing, whilst the 1 Lillie can be used turn 1 for a burst draw to 8 or later to refresh an emptied hand. The 1 Timer Ball and 1 Energy Loto provide flex options to search off “Mysterious Guidance”, Timer Ball notably does not force you to discard from hand, unlike Ultra Ball.
Elm for some combination of Ralts, Vulpix and Mudkip
Other Trainers

This deck plays a low 2 count of Guzma, owing to Gardevoir GX's uncapped damage. The 2 Choice Band help reach those high numbers either for less Energy or on the single-prize attackers in the deck. The 1 Judge keeps Zoroark and control decks from building and sitting on hands against you. Finally the 2 Max Potion allow you to heal a damaged Gardevoir GX, then accelerating Energy to it again to simply nullify the opponent's last attack.
Energy

To get enough value out of  “Secret Spring” and hit big numbers with Gardevoir GX, we need to play enough Fairy Energy. The deck therefore plays 7. It also plays 4 Double Colorless Energy which ramp said damage twice as fast and can allow Swampert to attack easier. The deck also plays one Super Boost Energy {*}, which can be used to add a massive 120 Damage to “Infinite Force” or allow Swampert to attack for 160.
